data_description.model: The brand and model of your heat pump or fan unit.

init.title: Heatpump Infrared options
init.description: IR emitters send commands one-way, so there's no built-in confirmation that the unit responded. Optionally point this at a temperature sensor near the unit so its reading is shown as the current temperature — giving you feedback that the unit is actually reacting, and, if you enable a control strategy below, so the integration can regulate the room against that sensor instead of the unit's own.

data_description.temperature_sensor_entity_id: A sensor entity reporting the room temperature near this unit. Leave blank to disable.
data_description.control_strategy: How the feedback sensor influences the unit. Display only: never override the unit. Offset compensation: keep the unit running but gradually bias the setpoint it's given so the room reaches your target instead of the unit's own sensor. Switch the unit off: send a power-off command when the target is reached, power back on when the room drifts out of band. Change the setpoint: slam the setpoint to its minimum (heating) or maximum (cooling) to stop the unit, then restore it. All except Display only require a feedback sensor.
data_description.control_deadband: How far past the target (in °C) the room must move before the integration reacts.
data_description.control_max_offset: The largest bias offset compensation may apply to the setpoint, in either direction.
data_description.control_interval: How long to wait between offset adjustments, giving the room time to respond.
